title: LinkedIn Public Profile Visibility Check | MyRecon

intro: LinkedIn's public-profile controls let you choose whether your profile and individual fields are eligible for display to people outside LinkedIn and in search tools. That is useful for balancing professional discovery with personal privacy, but search engines may take time to reflect a change. This guide shows how to inspect the current public view and make a measured change to your own account.

sections.heading: Open the public-profile controls
sections.body: LinkedIn Help directs desktop users through View Profile and the edit control beside Public profile & URL; on mobile it directs users through Settings, Visibility, and Edit your public profile. Review the master public-visibility choice and the separate field toggles. Choose the sections needed for your professional purpose rather than publishing every optional detail by habit.

sections.heading: Compare the settings with the outside view
sections.body: Inspect your own profile in a signed-out browser and, if relevant, a search result. LinkedIn notes that nonmembers may see a limited preview or be prompted to sign in even when the public profile is on. Record which page and context you actually observed instead of assuming every visitor sees the same fields.

sections.heading: Allow for search-engine delay
sections.body: LinkedIn warns that Google, Bing, and other search tools may take weeks or months to reflect public-profile changes. If a search result remains stale, confirm that the source page is updated first; then use the search provider's correction or removal tools where applicable. Do not describe a profile as still public solely because an old snippet persists.

sections.heading: Review reuse of your professional handle
sections.body: Search your own public LinkedIn handle with MyRecon and open each possible match at the original site. A repeated name or handle does not prove a shared owner. MyRecon's Android app is free and requires no signup, but its Google Play listing is currently in closed testing and access may be limited until release.

faq.question: Can I hide only some LinkedIn profile fields?
faq.answer: Yes. LinkedIn's public-profile help describes separate toggles for eligible profile information in addition to the main public-visibility setting. Review the individual fields in your own account because a limited preview may also depend on visitor context.

faq.question: Why does Google still show an old LinkedIn snippet?
faq.answer: LinkedIn says search tools can take weeks or months to detect profile changes and that LinkedIn does not control their refresh timing. Check the source profile first, then use the search provider's update process if the result remains outdated.

faq.question: Does turning off public visibility remove my LinkedIn account?
faq.answer: No. The public-visibility setting concerns eligibility for display outside LinkedIn and in search tools. It is not account deletion, and it should be checked separately from what signed-in LinkedIn members may see.

cta.label: Check your public username with MyRecon

takeaways: LinkedIn lets you control public-profile eligibility both for the full profile and for individual fields, so review each choice.
Compare your settings with a signed-out view and allow for search-engine delays before judging whether a change worked.
Use MyRecon to check public reuse of a professional handle, but require an original source before connecting accounts.
method: Use LinkedIn's official public-profile instructions for an account you control. Record the settings, signed-out source URL, search result if relevant, and date. Distinguish an updated LinkedIn page from a stale search snippet; treat any cross-site username match as a lead rather than identity proof.
